title: The Free Table
logline: On a dry-zone road with no restaurant in sight, a family that has fed passing strangers for free every day for years hands Chathura a plate before he even asks, and keeps insisting it was nothing.
human_question: What does it cost to give the same thing away, every day, to people who will never come back?

premise.story: A roadside family stall that feeds anyone who stops, with no fixed price and no memory kept of who paid and who didn't.
premise.place: A quiet stretch of dry-zone road between two towns, no restaurants for miles.
premise.experience: Arriving hungry and unknown, and being fed before being asked who you are.

concept_links.why: The eight wholesome sense-sphere minds cover both joyful, unprompted giving and calmer, habitual giving to a stranger who can never repay [C011-P:L89; C011-P:L93-L109].
The family's giving is not one single feeling but the ordinary team of goodness arriving together, unremarked and unnamed [C019-P:L49].

what_camera_could_observe: Lorries and buses slowing at the stall, the family's practised motions with no cash register
A stranger trying to pay and being waved off
The quiet after the road empties out
Family members eating what is left over at the end of the day
what_must_be_real: The family's actual business and economics of giving food away for free. No staged refusals or manufactured generosity for the camera.

possible_arc.opening: An empty road; a small stall lights up before dawn.
possible_arc.turn: Chathura tries to pay and is refused, and the family explains, or doesn't.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever the family actually says, if anything, about why they keep doing it.

position_hint: opening candidate: a natural, unstaged place for something to be given freely to Chathura, and for Object 6 to enter his hands, only if it really happens

requirements: A genuine roadside stall or household that feeds passing strangers without payment as an ongoing practice
Willingness to be filmed over enough time to show the pattern, not a single staged act
Real traffic and real strangers, not arranged visitors

suggestions.name: A road-side rest stop in the North Central dry zone
suggestions.why: This stretch has long-standing traditions of free wayside food and drink for travellers.
suggestions.verify: No specific stall or family has been identified or confirmed.

risks: Reducing a real, precarious business to a parable about kindness
The family's own economic fragility being glossed over
drop_if: No family or stall is found that genuinely gives food without payment as a matter of regular practice

connections.note: Both are ordinary, repeated acts of free giving to someone who cannot reciprocate, and both are candidates for where Object 6 first changes hands.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
